title: Nested-CV opponent-context regularization control
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The failed minimum-class and OOD-calibration gates arise mainly from the unregularized readout rather than insufficient public session features; session-index-disjoint cross-validation can select L2 and temperature without touching the final test, yielding at 64 hands at least 75% overall accuracy, 50% every-class accuracy, and 25% normalized entropy on SHA-disjoint unseen policies.
material_change: Reuse the exact hash-frozen 84 session-feature rows with zero new environment hands. Select L2 by eight-fold session-index OOF minimum-class accuracy then overall accuracy and NLL; select temperature only by OOF NLL; fit on all 48 selection rows and open the 24 untouched test plus 12 unseen holdout rows exactly once.
baseline: The unregularized readout reached 79.17% aggregate 64-hand accuracy but only 25% minimum-class accuracy and 0.00368 nats holdout entropy with 100% training accuracy.
notes: The 24 final test rows and 12 unseen-policy rows are sealed from hyperparameter and temperature selection. Passing this readout gate would admit a context representation mechanism only, not policy strength.

No new poker hands were generated. Model and temperature selection used only 48 selection sessions; 24 test sessions and 12 SHA-disjoint holdout sessions remained untouched until the final evaluation.

At 32 hands, overall accuracy passed but minimum-class accuracy remained 25%; any downstream policy prototype must treat the first 32 hands as insufficient context and preserve the base policy under uncertainty.

result.summary: Nested session-index CV selected L2=1 and temperature=1.1892 at 64 hands. The single untouched test reached 91.67% overall accuracy and 75% minimum-class accuracy, while SHA-disjoint holdout normalized entropy rose to 65.11%; all preregistered gates passed with zero new environment hands.
result.conclusion: Strong regularization and OOF-only calibration resolve the prior readout's breadth failure at 64 hands, so public cross-hand context is admitted as a feasible representation mechanism. The 32-hand minimum-class failure bounds the useful horizon, and no poker-policy strength claim follows from classifier accuracy alone.
result.next_step: Build a minimal Standard10-preserving context-conditioned learned residual pilot across multiple seeds and both seats, with a strict zero-context equivalence gate and untouched broad-league evaluation before any Slumbot use or geometric scaling.
